messages.subject: Got NA values when using summarise and one summarized column name is the prefix of the other
messages.subject_clean: Got NA values when using summarise and one summarized column name is the prefix of the other
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

recently, when I used plyr to convert some data, I got a whole column of NA values.
For simplicity, I make a toy test code to demonstrate what I encountered:
###########################################################################################
> > acc <- c(1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3)
> > ds <- rep(letters[1:3], each=3)
> > r <- data.frame(ds, acc)
> > s <- ddply(r, .(ds), summarise, acc=round(mean(acc), 4), acc.sd <http://acc.sd>=round(sd(acc), 4))
>
> > r
>   ds acc
> 1  a 1.1
> 2  a 1.2
> 3  a 1.3
> 4  b 2.1
> 5  b 2.2
> 6  b 2.3
> 7  c 3.1
> 8  c 3.2
> 9  c 3.3
>
> > s
>   ds acc acc.sd <http://acc.sd>
> 1  a 1.2     NA
> 2  b 2.2     NA
> 3  c 3.2     NA
###########################################################################################

However, When I change the first column name "acc" to something
that is not the prefix of the second column name, these NA values disappear.

###########################################################################################
> > s <- ddply(r, .(ds), summarise, accs=round(mean(acc), 4), acc.sd <http://acc.sd>=round(sd(acc), 4))
> > s
>   ds accs acc.sd <http://acc.sd>
> 1  a  1.2    0.1
> 2  b  2.2    0.1
> 3  c  3.2    0.1
###########################################################################################

messages.subject: Select verb on grouped_df
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I would like first to thank Hadley and Romain for excellent package 'dplyr'.
I was playing with manip verbs (filter, select, etc) and I experienced an error with select.

require(dplyr) ## latest version

group_by(mtcars, vs) %.% select(mpg)
Error: index out of bounds

str(group_by(mtcars, vs) %.% subset(select = mpg))
Classes ‘grouped_df’, ‘tbl_df’, ‘tbl’ and 'data.frame':    32 obs. of  1 variable:
 $ mpg: num  21 21 22.8 21.4 18.7 18.1 14.3 24.4 22.8 19.2 ...

It's a known issue or a desired feature of select ?

Thanks

Dear Hadley et al. –

messages.subject: dplyr, do , lm giving me empty lists.
messages.subject_clean: dplyr, do , lm giving me empty lists.
messages.body_plain:
Hi
I'm having difficulty using the dplyr do() function. I am closely following the help(do) example but each attempt using the in-built hflights data gives me a 0 length list. I jumped to the assumption that it was a problem with NA but now with the code below--  I don't think so. Here is what I have tried. NB Although tho si slightly different from the example(do),  that fails too on the similar last couple of lines.

# version 1.0 updated ~ Dec 26th
library(dplyr)

# this works
lm(Distance~AirTime, data=hflights, na.action="na.exclude")
Call:
  lm(formula = Distance ~ AirTime, data = hflights, na.action = "na.exclude")
Coefficients:
  (Intercept)      AirTime
-64.983        7.904

# with and without NA
carriers <- group_by(hflights, UniqueCarrier)
carriers.complete=group_by(hflights[complete.cases(hflights),], UniqueCarrier)

group_size(carriers)
[1]    79 73053  4648  2139   838  2204 45343  4082  2072 16061  2641 70032   695   365  3244

group_size(carriers.complete)
 [1]    78 71669  4504  2111   832  2121 44536  4030  2033 15781  2591 69373   673   364  3178

# all give 0 length lists
do(carriers, failwith(NULL, lm), formula = Distance ~ AirTime)
list()
do(carriers.complete, failwith(NULL, lm), formula = Distance ~ AirTime)
list()
do(carriers, failwith(NULL, lm), formula = Distance ~ AirTime, na.action="na.exclude")
list()
do(carriers, lm, formula = Distance ~ AirTime, na.action="na.exclude")
list()

# these are last couple of lines of example(do)
mods <- do(carriers, failwith(NULL, lm), formula = ArrDelay ~ date)
sapply(mods, coef)
list()
